A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quasar-driven outflows are the most important process in shaping the intergalactic gas distribution at early epochs, and that they may have been responsible for the formation of the first galaxies.
the formation of the first galaxies and the first globular clusters may be closely related.
the outflows from the quasars are able to remove a substantial amount of gas from the galaxies and to heat the intergalactic space, which can be seen in the cosmic microwave back-ground (CMB).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGM is a rich environment for the formation of dwarf and globular clusters.
the quasar outflow model is capable of explaining the formation of a significant fraction of the baryons in the universe at high redshifts, in addition to the formation of dwarf galaxy halos.
the IGM can become an important source of baryon supply for dwarf galaxies, which can then grow into normal-sized galaxies by subsequent accretion of the surrounding gas.
